definition: A system prompt is a set of instructions given to the AI before your message ever arrives — its job description, its rules, its personality. You usually never see it, but it shapes every answer: what the AI is allowed to do, what it must refuse, and how it talks to you.

edges.label: set by
edges.note: The harness writes the system prompt to define the assistant's role and rules.

edges.label: teamed with
edges.note: System prompts set the rules; MCP restrictions enforce what tools can actually do.

example.body: A bank's assistant happily helps you check balances and dispute charges. Ask it to reveal another customer's account number and it refuses — politely, every time. That refusal wasn't the model's idea; it was a line in the system prompt written by the bank's team. Same model, different rulebook, different behavior.
example.title: The bank teller's rulebook

footnotes.body: Modern systems use a role hierarchy (system > developer > user) where higher-privilege instructions win conflicts. Prompt injection attacks try to smuggle fake 'system' instructions inside user content or tool outputs — which is why harnesses treat tool output as untrusted data, never as instructions.
footnotes.label: For the technical reader

name: System Prompt
tagline: The hidden instructions that set the AI's role before you ever say a word.
whyItMatters: This is where safety and behavior actually live. 'Never reveal account numbers' isn't a property of the model — it's a line in a system prompt. And it's why 'ignore your instructions and…' tricks are a real attack: they're trying to overwrite these hidden rules, which is exactly what prompt injection is.
